title: Life OS
description: Tasks, projects, notes, goals and areas in one connected home with a daily view.
forWho: Anyone running their whole life from one place

spec.useCase: Camila Reyes keeps her work, health and money projects in one place and starts each morning from a short list of what matters.

text.text: One home for tasks, projects, notes and goals. Start with My day, capture anything new, and review the goals each week.
My day
Coming up
Projects
Goals
Notes and people
Start here each morning: what is overdue, what is due today, and what lands this week. Everything below reads live from your tasks.
Open high priority
Time logged
How to read this page
The task lists at the top are live: Today and Overdue are your morning check.
Minutes by energy shows when your focused time happens; protect the high-energy hours for deep work.
If Overdue keeps growing, shorten the next-actions list instead of adding more.
Thirty minutes, once a week, keeps the whole system trustworthy.
Clear
Empty the notes inbox into projects
Move finished tasks to Done
Pick the three tasks that matter most
Check
Scan projects that have no open task
Look at goal progress and milestone dates
Note one thing to drop
Plan
Flag next week's My day candidates
Block time for the biggest project
Message anyone you owe a reply
Questions worth answering
Which project moved most this week, and what made that possible?
Which goal has no open milestone in the next month?
What did I say yes to that I should have declined?
Keep a project alive with exactly one clearly written next action. A project with none is stalled, whatever its status says.
Example weekly note
Cleared nine notes. The Spring Garden project had no next action, so I added "measure the bed" for Saturday. Goal "Run a 10k" is behind: moved the long run to Sunday morning.
Areas are standards you maintain; goals are outcomes you chase. Keep both short.
Area example: Health. Standard: three workouts a week, sleep before midnight. Review: weekly.
Goal example: Run a 10k by spring. Milestones: 5k without stopping, 8k long run, race day.
Rule of thumb: an area never finishes; a goal always does.
Milestones
Work sessions
Using areas well
Give each area a written standard, such as "three workouts a week", so a review has something to measure against.
Set the review cadence to match how fast the area drifts: finances monthly, health weekly.
A goal without a milestone in the next 30 days is stalling; add the next one.
